newsitem.title: NORWAY: Sparebankgruppen extends bid for Fokus.
newsitem.headline: Sparebankgruppen extends bid for Fokus.

text.p: Sparebankgruppen, a group of Norwegian savings banks, said on Friday it was extending by six weeks a takeover bid to shareholders in Fokus Bank.
Sparebankgruppen, whose 73 crowns per share bid is seen as hostile by the Fokus Bank board, said it now controls 51 percent of Norway's fourth largest bank.

Sparebankgruppen, whose bid was to have expired on Friday at 1400 GMT, said: "Sparebankgruppen AS has won acceptance from about 51 percent of the shares in Fokus Bank and extends the bid period by six weeks."
It said the figure of 51 percent included own acquisitions, options and acceptance declarations from shareholders in Fokus.
The new deadline was set for Friday July 18 at 1400 GMT. The terms otherwise were left unchanged.
Earlier on Friday, Fokus said it had agreed to sell its 10 percent stake in BNbank ASA to Den norske Bank ASA (DnB).
The announcement effectively ended Fokus' attempt to take over BNbank, a niche mortgage lender, and paved the way for DnB to acquire it.
Fokus had previously refused to sell the shares to DnB, with which it fought a bitter battle for BNbank.
Fokus also said DnB had agreed not to sell its 8.49 percent shareholding in Fokus to Sparebankgruppen, whose bid is seen as hostile by the board of Fokus.
Analysts said the agreement betwen Fokus and DnB was a trade-off under which DnB was ensured ownership of BNbank at the same time as Sparebankgruppen is denied a considerable stake in Fokus.
Fokus has recommended its shareholders to turn down the takeover bid by Sparebankgruppen, which wants to carve up Fokus among its 16 members.
DnB, Norway's largest bank, last month submitted a formal application to the Finance Ministry -- the regulatory body -- for permission to take over BNbank.
